verdict: OK to lend in Unnao meat & poultry processing — back integrated processors and cold-chain buyers only; avoid sub-scale wet shops and export-dependent units
title: Unnao meat & poultry processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A meat/poultry processor buys live birds or animals, converts them through slaughter, chilling/freezing and packing, and sells into local wet markets, HORECA and frozen retail.** Cash sits in live inventory and receivables from distributors; value sits in cold-chain and shelf life, not in the killing floor. **Feed is the largest cost line, so margin is a feed-price and live-weight game, not a pricing game** — ICRA notes raw material is the largest component of cost for such FMCG-linked businesses [9]. Longer frozen shelf life partly shields realisations from broiler price swings [10]. For Unnao specifically, the local sources say almost nothing usable about the processing cluster, so lean on first principles and peers.

Peer results are mixed-to-positive: Venky's poultry revenue rose from INR 1,755 crore in FY24 to INR 1,927 crore in FY25, 10% growth [4], and Mayank Cattle Food reported higher H1 FY27 revenue on demand and efficiency [5]. **UP GST collections are running +14.2% Apr-to-date vs India +6.1% [D], a genuine local demand tailwind.** But India bank credit is +26.3% YoY against output +5.1% [D] — money is chasing this sector faster than it is producing, so underwriting discipline matters more than appetite.

## Where to grow
**Pursue integrated processors with own feed/hatchery linkage, cold-chain owners, and B2B suppliers to frozen retail and HORECA.** Venky's model — feed, breeder, hatchery, processing, ready-to-cook [10] — is the template; look for borrowers copying even two of those stages. **Avoid standalone wet shops, units with temple-adjacent or unlicensed premises [3], and any borrower whose sales depend on a single export destination.** When a proposal lands, check the licence and municipal clearance first; if the shop is unlicensed or contested, decline regardless of cash flow.

## How to grow safely
**Structure as working-capital-led: cash credit against live inventory and receivables, with a term loan only for cold storage or processing line.** Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, monthly feed purchase invoices, and quarterly GST returns. **Covenant on feed cost as a share of sales and on inventory days; if feed share jumps, ask for the revised pricing and buyer contracts.** Rating reports show strong groups run large undrawn working capital buffers [8] — insist on the same headroom here.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch live-weight purchase prices, cold-store electricity bills, and buyer concentration.** If a borrower's top buyer crosses a third of sales, ask for a second-buyer contract before enhancing limits. If municipal or social pressure on premises appears [3], freeze fresh disbursement and inspect the site.
watch: Inventory days rise beyond borrower's own 6-month average -> ask for ageing and hold enhancement
Feed cost share of sales jumps -> reprice or seek buyer pass-through proof
Filing gap or turnover fall vs bank credits -> site visit within 15 days
Any closure or dispute notice [3] -> freeze disbursement, inspect site
